potential.say: have potential · reach your full potential
ex: Your son has a lot of potential.
Does this new shop have potential?
I see great potential in this plan.
She can reach her full potential here.
potential.note: Often an adjective: "potential buyers." As a noun, uncountable: "She has a lot of potential."

department.say: work in a department · the sales department
ex: Which department do you work in?
Please call the sales department.
She works in the IT department.
Our department has a meeting every Monday.
department.note: Also a part of a store or a university: "the shoe department," "the English department."

trail.say: a hiking trail · on the trail
ex: This trail goes up the mountain.
Is this trail good for kids?
We walk on the forest trail every Sunday.
Can you show me the trail on the map?

sports bar.say: at a sports bar · watch the game at a sports bar
ex: Let's watch the game at a sports bar tonight.
Is there a good sports bar near the hotel?
The sports bar on our street has ten big TVs.
We met our friends at a sports bar after work.

cheating.say: cheating on a test · accuse someone of cheating
ex: Cheating on a test is against school rules.
The teacher saw no cheating during the exam.
Using a phone in the exam is cheating.
In online games, cheating can get your account banned.
cheating.note: Often a verb form: "He is cheating." "Cheating on" a partner means being unfaithful.

ex: Motherfucker is one of the rudest words in English.
Never call your boss a motherfucker, even as a joke.
In the movie, the angry driver shouts "motherfucker" many times.
Friends sometimes say motherfucker as a joke, but it's rude.
motherfucker.note: Very rude and offensive; avoid it. Friends may use it as a joke, but it is still vulgar.

ex: The German chancellor will visit Kyiv next week.
The chancellor leads the government in Germany and Austria.
Who was chancellor of Germany before the last election?
The new chancellor will speak on TV tonight.
chancellor.note: Also the head of some US universities, and the UK finance minister ("Chancellor of the Exchequer").

ex: I do a short workout every morning before work.
How long is your workout at the gym?
This workout is hard, but it makes my legs strong.
Drink some water after your workout.
Our team uses a popular web framework for the site.
Which framework do you use for your mobile apps?
A good framework helps developers write code faster.
She is learning a new framework for building websites.
framework.note: Most often "framework" means a basic structure or set of rules: "a legal framework."

ex: Press this keyboard shortcut to copy the text.
Is there a shortcut for saving the file?
I put a shortcut to the program on my desktop.
Learning a few shortcuts makes work on a computer faster.
shortcut.note: Most often "shortcut" means a shorter way: "We took a shortcut through the park."

ex: A national liberal supports both a strong nation and free markets.
In the 19th century, many national liberals wanted one united Germany.
The national liberals won several seats in the election.
He called himself a national liberal in the interview.
The tour guide told us not to enter the sex theater.
The old sex theater on this street is closed now.
You must be over eighteen to go into a sex theater.
The city wants to close the sex theater near the school.
Our class started a wiki project about local birds.
Anyone can help with this wiki project online.
The wiki project needs more volunteers to check facts.
She runs a wiki project about the history of our town.
National liberalism was popular in Europe in the 19th century.
Our history teacher explained national liberalism with simple examples.
National liberalism mixes love for the nation with free markets.
Many parties in Germany once supported national liberalism.
After the factory closed, the town was in stasis for years.
In the movie, the crew sleeps in stasis during the long trip.
The project is in stasis until we get more money.
The market stayed in stasis, with no prices going up or down.
stasis.note: Uncountable and formal: "in stasis" means not changing or moving at all.
